## Hexagonal Architecture (Ports & Adapters)

- Organize code into three layers: **Domain** (core business logic), **Application** (use cases), and **Infrastructure** (external integrations).
- Domain layer **MUST** have zero dependencies on frameworks, databases, or external services — it contains only pure business logic.
- Define **Ports** as interfaces in the Domain layer for all external interactions — input ports for use cases, output ports for persistence and messaging.
- Implement **Adapters** in the Infrastructure layer — they fulfill Port contracts using framework-specific code (HTTP controllers, ORM repositories, message brokers).
- Application layer orchestrates use cases by calling Domain logic through Port interfaces — **NEVER** call Adapters directly from the Application layer.
- **NEVER** import from Infrastructure into Domain — all dependency arrows **MUST** point inward toward the Domain core.
- Use Dependency Injection to wire Adapters to Ports at application startup — the composition root is the only place that knows about concrete implementations.
